briefs.title: install counter concurrency testing
briefs.description: Use install counter concurrency testing to prove simultaneous add events increment installCount and weeklyInstalls without lost updates under load.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove simultaneous install events increment installCount and weeklyInstalls without lost updates?

outline.heading: What Must Install Counter Concurrency Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the invariant that N resolved add events produce N install rows and increase both counters by N.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a Postgres Atomic Increment Test?
outline.coverage: Send simultaneous requests and verify SQL column-plus-one expressions preserve every committed increment.

outline.heading: What Exposes a Lost Update Install Counter?
outline.coverage: Contrast atomic updates with a read-modify-write fixture and use expected versus actual deltas as the oracle.

outline.heading: Drizzle Concurrent Update Testing
outline.coverage: Coordinate a request barrier, release a known concurrency level, and inspect affected rows, counters, and event inserts.

outline.heading: How Do You Reproduce a Weekly Installs Race Condition?
outline.coverage: Set both counters to different starting values and assert each receives the same delta after the concurrent burst.

outline.heading: Telemetry Counter Load Test Scope
outline.coverage: Separate correctness at moderate concurrency from performance benchmarking and report request failures before interpreting counter totals.

outline.heading: Concurrency Level, Rows, and Counter Delta Matrix
outline.coverage: Present sequential and parallel loads with accepted requests, install rows, expected counters, and observed loss.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Concurrent Increment Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed, synchronize, burst, await all responses, query side effects, and repeat with independent fixtures.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about atomic SQL, transactions, request errors, replay protection, database pools, weekly resets, and flaky timing.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the event-to-counter invariant and direct readers to telemetry and database testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to verify concurrent counter increments
steps: Seed one skill with known, unequal values in both counters.
Prepare N valid add events that all resolve to the same skill.
Release all POST calls from one synchronization barrier.
Await every response and fail if any request did not complete.
Query install rows and both counters in one verification step.
Assert every delta equals N and repeat the run with a fresh fixture.

codeExamples.focus: Exercise the insert and atomic SQL increment under parallel POST requests.

codeExamples.title: Seed and verify both counters
codeExamples.focus: Use explicit installCount and weeklyInstalls baselines to detect any lost update.

briefs.title: review comment length validation testing
briefs.description: Use review comment length validation testing to cover the 1,000-unit boundary, whitespace, emoji, surrogate pairs, and off-by-one inputs in APIs.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test the 1,000-character review limit with empty text, whitespace, emoji, surrogate pairs, and boundary values?

outline.heading: What Must Review Comment Length Validation Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the current JavaScript length contract, conditional validation, accepted empty values, and 1,000-unit inclusive boundary.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a 1000 Character Comment Test?
outline.coverage: Generate deterministic strings at 999, 1,000, and 1,001 UTF-16 code units and assert status plus database writes.

outline.heading: What Does an Emoji String Length API Measure?
outline.coverage: Explain JavaScript UTF-16 length with single-code-unit text, surrogate pairs, and multi-code-point grapheme clusters.

outline.heading: Review Whitespace Validation Cases
outline.coverage: Test empty string, spaces, tabs, line breaks, and long whitespace because the route checks length but does not trim or require content.

outline.heading: How Do You Run Unicode Boundary Value Testing?
outline.coverage: Construct code-unit-controlled fixtures and report visible characters separately from JavaScript length.

outline.heading: Comment Limit Off by One Assertions
outline.coverage: Prove exactly 1,000 is accepted and 1,001 is rejected with no review row, while missing text persists as empty.

outline.heading: Input Text, Code Units, and Expected Response Matrix
outline.coverage: Present ASCII, whitespace, emoji, combining sequence, and boundary values with visible length, code units, status, and stored value.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement the Comment Boundary Procedure?
outline.coverage: Use a fresh authenticated user per accepted review, table-driven generators, and row-count checks for rejected values.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about characters versus code units, emoji, whitespace, trimming, database text limits, normalization, and error responses.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Restate the actual code-unit boundary and direct readers to API validation skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test review comment length
steps: Create authenticated user and skill fixtures for POST requests.
Generate inputs with explicit JavaScript lengths around 1,000.
POST each rejected input and assert the exact 400 response.
Verify rejected cases do not insert review rows.
POST accepted ASCII, whitespace, and Unicode boundary cases with fresh users.
Query the rows and assert the exact stored comment values.

codeExamples.focus: Exercise comment.length, conditional validation, and comment-or-empty persistence.

codeExamples.title: Assert text storage at accepted boundaries
codeExamples.focus: Verify PostgreSQL stores accepted whitespace and Unicode strings without test-side normalization.

briefs.title: Postgres ILIKE wildcard escaping
briefs.description: Use Postgres ILIKE wildcard escaping tests to cover percent, underscore, backslash, Unicode, and literal substring search expectations in APIs.
briefs.coreQuestion: How should QA test percent, underscore, backslash, and Unicode input in a Drizzle ILIKE substring search?

outline.heading: What Must Postgres ILIKE Wildcard Escaping Tests Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the current percent-wrapped pattern and distinguish intended substring search from user-supplied wildcard expansion.

outline.heading: How Do You Escape Percent in ILIKE?
outline.coverage: Test literal percent values against rows with and without percent signs, then compare current wildcard behavior with an escaped contract.

outline.heading: What Is a Postgres Underscore Wildcard Test?
outline.coverage: Use one-character substitutions around underscores to prove whether input is treated as a pattern or literal text.

outline.heading: Drizzle Substring Search Edge Cases
outline.coverage: Cover empty query, percent, underscore, backslash, quotes, mixed wildcards, long input, and matching across name and description.

outline.heading: How Does Unicode Case Insensitive Search Behave?
outline.coverage: Use database collation-aware fixtures and avoid universal case-folding claims beyond the configured PostgreSQL behavior.

outline.heading: ILIKE Backslash Escape Testing
outline.coverage: Test literal backslashes and escaped wildcard sequences with explicit expected rows under the chosen escape strategy.

outline.heading: Query Input, SQL Pattern, and Match Matrix
outline.coverage: Present raw input, interpolated pattern, fixture values, current matches, literal-intent matches, and assertion purpose.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Wildcard Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed discriminating text, call the skills endpoint, capture result IDs, and compare current and escaped expectations without constructing raw SQL.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about SQL injection, parameterization, percent, underscore, backslash, collation, Unicode, and empty queries.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the literal-versus-pattern decision and link to database search testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test ILIKE wildcard input
steps: Seed skill names and descriptions that isolate percent, underscore, backslash, and Unicode cases.
Call the skills API with each raw query value.
Record the returned skill IDs and compare them with the current pattern semantics.
Define the intended literal or wildcard product contract explicitly.
Implement escaping only if the product contract requires literal matching.
Rerun the same fixture matrix and assert exact result sets.

codeExamples.focus: Send special query characters through both name and description conditions.

codeExamples.title: Seed discriminating searchable text
codeExamples.focus: Create rows that separate wildcard matches from literal substring matches.

briefs.title: Redis cached null ambiguity testing
briefs.description: Use Redis cached null ambiguity testing to distinguish a missing key, a stored null value, a read failure, and a source fetch in cache helpers.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test a cache helper that uses null for both a missing key and a legitimately cached null value?

outline.heading: What Must Redis Cached Null Ambiguity Testing Expose?
outline.coverage: Define four states that collapse to null in the current helper: no client, missing key, read exception, and stored null.

outline.heading: How Do You Write a Redis Null Cache Miss Test?
outline.coverage: Stub each read outcome and count source fetcher calls to prove which values the helper treats as misses.

outline.heading: What Is a Negative Caching Sentinel Value?
outline.coverage: Compare tagged objects, explicit hit wrappers, and sentinel strings that preserve the distinction between cached null and absence.

outline.heading: CacheGetOrSet Nullable Data Cases
outline.coverage: Use fetchers returning null, objects, zero, false, and empty strings to verify only strict null receives miss semantics.

outline.heading: How Do You Distinguish Cached Null Versus Missing Key?
outline.coverage: Use EXISTS or a tagged envelope in the proposed contract and test that each state has an independent observable result.

outline.heading: TypeScript Generic Cache Ambiguity
outline.coverage: Show why Promise<T | null> cannot encode hit status when T itself includes null and define a discriminated result type.

outline.heading: Redis State, Helper Result, and Fetcher Call Matrix
outline.coverage: Present key state, Redis response, cacheGet output, cacheGetOrSet action, source calls, and preferred representation.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Null Ambiguity Procedure?
outline.coverage: Test current behavior first, add the chosen explicit state contract, and rerun missing, null, error, and non-null cases.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about negative caching, EXISTS, null serialization, falsy values, read errors, TTL, and generic types.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the need for explicit cache state and link to cache-testing resources.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test cached null semantics
steps: Create a fetcher spy that returns a controlled nullable value.
Stub Redis for a missing key, stored null, read exception, false, and object.
Call cacheGetOrSet and record fetcher calls plus returned values.
Assert the current implementation treats all null outcomes as misses.
Introduce an explicit hit or miss representation in the proposed design.
Repeat the matrix and prove cached null no longer triggers the fetcher.

codeExamples.focus: Stub no client, missing key, stored null, read error, and non-null values.

codeExamples.title: Observe nullable caching through a real consumer
codeExamples.focus: Use a cacheGetOrSet caller to demonstrate fetcher invocation and response behavior.

briefs.title: review API pagination load testing
briefs.description: Use review API pagination load testing to measure latency, payload growth, database work, and client rendering when every review is returned.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test latency, payload size, and client rendering when the review GET endpoint returns every matching row without a limit?

outline.heading: What Must Review API Pagination Load Testing Measure?
outline.coverage: Define server latency, query duration, row count, response bytes, parse time, rendered items, and memory without inventing performance thresholds.

outline.heading: How Do You Run an Unpaginated Review Endpoint Load Test?
outline.coverage: Seed increasing review counts, request one skill at controlled concurrency, and capture distributions plus errors for each dataset size.

outline.heading: What Drives Large Review Response Performance?
outline.coverage: Trace joined user fields, ordered review rows, aggregate query, JSON serialization, transfer, parsing, and component mapping.

outline.heading: API Payload Growth Testing
outline.coverage: Measure bytes per row across short and long comments and verify totalReviews agrees with the unpaginated list.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a Review List Rendering Benchmark?
outline.coverage: Render the client component with controlled arrays and measure commit time and DOM item count separately from network time.

outline.heading: Database Query Without Limit QA
outline.coverage: Verify the source query has no cursor or limit, inspect its plan at representative sizes, and define a pagination acceptance target.

outline.heading: Review Count, Payload, and Latency Results Table
outline.coverage: Present dataset size, comment profile, response bytes, server latency, browser parse or render time, and errors.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the End-to-End Load Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed, warm, sample, collect, render, clean up, and compare against a paginated design using the same data.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about pagination thresholds, averages, cursor design, load versus stress tests, rendering, payload compression, and test data.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Turn measured growth into a pagination decision and link to performance and API skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to load test the unpaginated review flow
steps: Seed one skill with review datasets that increase by a fixed order of magnitude.
Warm the application and database before collecting samples.
Request GET repeatedly at controlled concurrency and record status, bytes, and timing.
Render each returned array in the review component and measure item count and commit time.
Inspect the database query plan for representative large datasets.
Compare results with an explicit paginated prototype using the same fixtures.

codeExamples.title: Measure the unbounded review GET route
codeExamples.focus: Capture response size and timing for the query without limit or cursor.

codeExamples.title: Benchmark client review mapping
codeExamples.focus: Render controlled review arrays and measure DOM growth separately from API latency.

briefs.cta: Browse API and performance testing skills at /skills before setting a review pagination target.
